posts.cooked:
Someone posting on the Handelabra forums had an interesting situation come up:

I noticed an interesting behavior, perhaps not a bug, but definitely not what I was expecting. I was playing against Citizen Dawn with Visionary on the team, and Visionary had a Decoy Projection in play. The decoy had the lowest number of hit points on the team. Citizen Autumn came into play and targeted the decoy as the lowest hitpoint hero. Fair enough. Autumn then destroyed all of the ongoing cards belonging to Visionary. That surprised me. I would have guessed that Autumn would try to strip the ongoing cards from the decoy, and since the decoy had no ongoing cards that Autumn's attack would have had no effect. Is it the correct behavior that Autumn's attack targets the decoy but actually hits Visionary?

The wording on Autumn does seem a bit ambiguous.  She goes after "the hero with the lowest HP".  The existence of The Sentinels, in particular, complicates things.

Possible interpretations that I see:

1) read the ambiguous text as "the hero with the lowest HP Hero Character Card".

2) read the ambiguous text as "the hero with the lowest HP Hero Target Card".

 

1 feels right to me, but it's a wacky enough circumstance that I'd like to hear other opinions.  Or is there an interpretation I'm missing?

posts.cooked: The Sentinels is the Hero. This is why if something targets only Heroes, it would target only one of The Sentinels. However if something targeted Hero Character Cards, it would target each of them. This is why only one member of The Sentinels can be infected at any given time and why Proverbs and Axioms allows each of them to heal or use a power.

I had a question about Visionary, don't know if here is the most appropriate place but here goes;

  1. Visionary has her Decoy card out  
  2. She plays Brain Burn.
  3. There are more than 5 cards in the villain deck.

The question I had was which of the following two thing happens?

A. Visionary deals damage to the Decoy until it is destroyed. She then stops dealing damage (because the target was destroyed).

B. Visionary deals damage until the decoy is destroyed and then deals the remaining damage to herself.

posts.name: Matchstickman
posts.cooked: Neither. The answer is C, all the damage is dealt to the decoy projection in one huge lump, the 'packet of damage' is directed to the decoy projection and then its HP is reduced, not one HP at a time but in a single hit, even if that takes it to negative HP (it is of course destroyed after the damage is done if this happens).

posts.name: MigrantP
posts.cooked:
The important bit is the wording on Brain Burn. She deals herself X psychic damage, where X is the number of cards. That's why it's one "packet of damage." 

There are other cards that have different wording, and work the way you expected. Take a look at Omnitron's Technological Singularity. It says Omnitron deals 2 lightning damage for each card destroyed. If 3 cards are destroyed, then it deals 2 lightning damage 3 times (and each one is modified separately).

If the Visionary has Decoy Projection out and a card like Technological Singularity attacks her, it would work like B).

posts.name: bluedarky
posts.cooked:
Ameena:

Yeah, stuff can go into negative hp, hence on some villains it says stuff happens when they're reduced to "zero or fewer hp". This doesn't tend to make much difference unless Fixed Point is out, in which case the target might manage to heal itself back up above zero and thus not instantly drop dead the moment Fixed Point goes away :).

It's also why villains who flip when reduced to zero specify "restore <villain> to X HP" and "not heal <villain> by X HP", because if by some fluke a hero managed to deal, say, 31 damage to a Baron Blade on 1 HP his Vengful Mad Scientist side would die instantly if it was the second.
